claims.text: In high-entropy alloys outside established Nb-Ta and titanium-rich systems, superconductivity is governed by the degree of local crystallographic ordering.
Local crystallographic ordering modulates electron-phonon coupling.
Enhanced local order produces more coherent phonon modes.
More coherent phonon modes yield a higher superconducting transition temperature.
Controlled thermal annealing can promote local atomic ordering without destroying the disordered single-phase solid solution.
Annealing-induced local ordering reduces random atomic-scale electron scattering.
Annealing-induced local ordering promotes coherent lattice vibrations.
The resulting coherent lattice vibrations enhance electron-phonon interactions involved in Cooper-pair formation.
Enhanced electron-phonon interactions increase the superconducting transition temperature.
Annealed samples with increased local order will have a higher superconducting transition temperature than as-cast, fully disordered samples.
Annealed samples with increased local order will have a larger superconducting gap than as-cast, fully disordered samples.
The as-cast alloy has a lower superconducting transition temperature because maximal atomic randomness causes stronger electron scattering.
The proposed relationship applies only when the alloy remains a single-phase solid solution after annealing.
Annealing-induced phase separation may change the predicted superconducting response.
Excessive ordering can undermine disorder needed for homogeneous superconductivity.
